verdict.rationale: Checkout.com's Flow is marketed as letting merchants accept payments using customizable components, and Flow for Mobile ships through native iOS and Android SDKs, so the product itself provides component-based checkout for in-app mobile use. The evidence is only marketing-level, though: it never explicitly says Flow embeds on the merchant's own web page rather than redirecting, and it never details what can be customized. missing for 10: explicit documentation that Flow web components embed in the merchant's own page without redirect, detail on customization scope (styling, layout, payment-method selection), and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can embed customizable payment components directly in my own site or app instead of redirecting to a hosted page

citations.quote: Accept payments using customizable components – all through one simple integration.
Take charge of your mobile checkout with Flow for Mobile. Available via iOS and Android Mobile SDKs.
Mobile SDK: Build native mobile checkout experiences for iOS and Android.
